presentation.label: 128 arrangements per project
presentation.summary: 16 books of 8 arrangements per project, every one a stock arrangement file: book 1 is arr01 to arr08, book 16 is arr121 to arr128.
presentation.overview: Songbook turns the Octatrack's 8 arrangements into 16 books of 8. Book 1 is stock's own arr01 to arr08 and stays exactly as it is; book 2 is arr09 to arr16, and so on up to arr128, all ordinary stock arrangement files in the project folder, written and read by the Octatrack's own code. In ARR > CHANGE, with the transport stopped, LEFT and RIGHT step through the books; inside a book every stock arrangement function works as usual. Setlists of up to 16 songs from any books follow in a later version.
highlights: Every arrangement is a stock file, arr01 to arr128.
Switch books with LEFT/RIGHT in ARR > CHANGE, stopped.
A project opens on book 1, also on a unit without the module.
usage: Open ARR > CHANGE (MKII: ARR, then CHANGE; MKI: FUNC + PATTERN for arrangement mode, FUNC + BANK, then CHANGE), with the transport stopped.
Press RIGHT or LEFT to step to the next or previous book (1 to 16); BOOK 2 and so on shows at the top right.
Pick one of the book's 8 arrangements as usual and edit, save or chain it: stock's arrangement functions work inside the book.
Save the project as usual: every book is saved with it.
Before removing the module, step back to book 1.

limitations: OS 1.40C, tested on an MKI (the developer's own checks, build f068cd608, base 0.7.13); not tested on an MKII.
Books change only while the transport is stopped: the switch writes and reads the card, which stock itself does only stopped.

Switch back to book 1 before removing the module: without it, stock's next save writes the book in use into arr01 to arr08. Book 1 is kept in a backup (arr01.bak to arr08.bak) and comes back the next time the module is installed and book 1 is chosen.
A project comes back to the book and arrangement it was saved or left on; a power cycle keeps the book in use. Without the module a project opens on book 1.
Stock's project copy functions copy book 1 only; copying the project folder copies every book.

impact.conditions: A book switch at its dearest (book 1 to another, stopped): stock's save of arr01-08, book 1's backup, the next book read and the slots fingerprinted. Between switches the UI tick re-fingerprints the slots every 2 s off book 1.

cpu.rationale: A switch runs inside stock's SYNC TO CARD job, stopped: 13.8 million executed ColdFire instructions under ot_emu from book 1 to 2, 7.8 million back, most of it stock's own file writes and reads. Off book 1 the UI tick fingerprints the 8 slots every 2 s (about 543,000 instructions, counted from the unit). Time on the unit is not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code: the module only switches which arrangements stock's own player has in its 8 slots.

memory.rationale: 7,292 bytes of ColdFire code and data and 4,728 of state, plus a 20-byte battery RAM record; on the card, stock arrangement files for books 2-16, book 1's backup and a 24-byte place file per project.

tests.summary: Host gate (verify.py, 97 checks, a missing, unreadable or partly written book 1 backup, a file that fails to open once and a reload after it among them; several replaying the unit's event orders and stock's two load jobs); stock's file format for arr09 and up, the list redraw and per-book choice under ot_emu. On the developer's MKI (OS 1.40C): switching books 1-16, per-book choice, the playing refusal, ARR SAVE/RELOAD, FUNC + PLAY clears and their undo, a power cycle and arranger mode after LOAD (build c5027552c, base 0.7.5); LOAD and RELOAD returning to book 2 in arranger mode with book 1 intact, the main screen and PLAY on the returned book (build f068cd608, base 0.7.13, beside USB AUDIO), as the developer reported them; distinct books 1 and 2 kept through a power cycle and through a trial of another build with Undo, each followed by SYNC TO CARD (build b976e98ff, package 37f7e94f, base 0.7.13), as the developer reported them; a LOAD of another project and back, each on its own book and arrangement with the list cursor on it, PLAY and LEFT/RIGHT after it (build 85d544a68, package 81eb7172, base 0.7.13), as the developer reported them.

conditions.parameterExtremes: The dearest event is a book switch away from book 1: stock's writer saves arr01-08, the module writes book 1's backup (arr01.bak-arr08.bak) and reads the next book's 8 files, then fingerprints the 8 slots (90,440 bytes). 13,754,188 instructions from the writer's entry (0x400915ac) to its return (0x40091a76) on book 1 to 2; book 2 to 1 (backup read back) 7,849,450.
conditions.parameterModulation: Not applicable: no parameters or audio; one switch per LEFT/RIGHT press in ARR > CHANGE, stopped, or one return after a project load.
conditions.modeSwitching: Both directions measured; a switch between two other books writes and reads 8 files each and no backup, so it lies between the two.
conditions.maxLoad: Executed ColdFire instructions under ot_emu, interrupts and every other task in that window included; one instance (the module is project-wide). Budget: 100 ms of ColdFire time at 266 MHz, a responsiveness target for a key press, as Apply Scene's; the switch runs inside stock's SYNC TO CARD job on the card task, refused while playing.
conditions.inputConditions: Empty arrangements; the arrangement blocks are fixed-size, so their content does not change the writes, reads or the fingerprint. Executed instructions, not cycles: cache and wait states are not modelled, and card time on the unit is not measured.

regions.name: ColdFire code and data (one linked unit)

memory.conditions: The unit as the USB package carries it: 7,292 bytes of code and data and 4,728 of bss (the builder's report), plus the 20-byte battery RAM record at 0x100f8f10. On the card: arr09.work-arr128.work and their .strd copies (stock arrangement files), arr01.bak-arr08.bak and arrbook.work/.strd in the project folder. No DSP memory.

hardware.summary: On the developer's Octatrack MKI (OS 1.40C, base 0.7.13 6d23e888), this exact package kept over USB beside USB AUDIO and Arr Rows: switching books, the per-book choice with the CHANGE list's cursor and YES on it after a switch and after closing and reopening the list, a LOAD of another project and back (each on its own book and arrangement, one card job of the module's, no NOW SAFE TO EJECT!), PLAY from the returned arrangement. Earlier builds of the same lineage covered SAVE/RELOAD PROJECT, ARR SAVE/RELOAD, FUNC + PLAY clears and undo, a power cycle and arranger mode (TESTING.md). As the developer reported them.
limitations: The test procedure's scripted pass, soak and cost on the unit (steps 7-9) have not run yet (#2099, fixed in #2103); a trial of this package under the scripted pass ran about two minutes twice with no crash, stall, freeze or skipped track.
Removing the module on a book other than 1 is a documented limitation, not tested.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: In ARR > CHANGE, press RIGHT: BOOK 2, with 8 empty arrangements.
Choose arrangement 1, open the editor and add a few rows.
Back in ARR > CHANGE, press LEFT: BOOK 1, your original arrangements.
Press RIGHT again: book 2's rows are back.
Press LEFT to return to book 1 before you finish.
